A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniCode, with matching core pipelines, benchmark results, and substantial appendix material. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite retitling and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, human problem ratings, test-generation ablations, and generalization experiments, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds augmentation-specific evaluations, error analyses, recursive augmentation, and test-suite composition and generator-bias experiments.

M1.justification: The underlying extension/fusion and brute-force/filtering/consensus pipelines remain. Beyond renaming, Appendix B.8 constrains generation prompts to explicit variation strategies, adds balanced rule/scale selection and variation labels, and specifies a five-second feasibility constraint. Section 5.2 and Appendix B.9 add an LLM-based error-labeling procedure.

E1.justification: The competitive-programming domain, seed sources, and algorithmic taxonomy remain. V2 adds second-generation recursive variants, extending evaluation to cumulative structural and logical shifts beyond v1's seed, shadow, and first-generation comparisons (Appendix A.5).

E2.justification: The controlled generalization comparison expands from four models in v1 Figure 3 to eight in v2 Figure 3, with substantial membership changes: Claude Sonnet 4 and Qwen3-Coder-Flash appear instead of Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Qwen3-235B-A22B, alongside additional models. The main leaderboard and rStar-Coder comparison retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: V2 replaces RandPass/AdvPass reporting with leave-one-input-source-out impacts, increases human evaluation from 50 to 113 problems, and introduces recursive, suite-composition, and generator-comparison protocols. Section 4.1 reports two benchmark generators, whereas Appendices A.3/B.3 still describe the standard benchmark as o4-mini-generated; the PDFs do not establish whether the retained leaderboard was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds augmentation-axis diagnostics, error distributions and failure case studies, algorithm-combination heatmaps, recursive robustness testing, a test-suite composition sweep, and generator-bias analysis. These substantially expand the questions investigated. The original stress-pipeline ablations are retained in Appendix B.1.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly states that random seeds are stored in per-case provenance; v2 omits this seed-information disclosure. Existing correlation significance reporting and the appendix confidence-bound treatment remain. No increase in repeated runs or new empirical uncertainty-estimation practice is established.

E6.justification: All 21 main leaderboard rows retain their difficulty and overall percentages. V2 adds extensive diagnostic, recursive, generator-comparison, and suite-sweep results, including o4-mini's 55.6% efficiency-scaling accuracy. Human validity is reported as 98.2% on 113 problems instead of 98.0% on 50. V1's per-model output-token results are removed; the new settings do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The test-impact quantity is redefined from AdvPass minus RandPass in v1 Table 2 to overall performance minus performance without a particular input source in v2 Table 1. Otherwise, the contamination model, bias/variance and confidence-bound derivations, and algorithm-capacity calculations are mathematically retained in Appendices B.5–B.6.

C1.justification: V2 shifts the central contribution from generating high-quality competitive problems toward diagnosing code reasoning through targeted augmentation. Fine-grained failure diagnosis, seed-problem regression, and deficiencies in conceptual modeling and scalability become explicit abstract, introduction, and conclusion claims. The scalable test-generation contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving seed-logic regression, cascading errors, and different roles for memorization and reasoning across augmentation depths. It interprets generator differences as stylistic preferences and uses benchmark correlations to support stronger contamination-resistance and unbiasedness claims. These go beyond v1's interpretations and its explicitly untested single-generator limitation.

D1.justification: V2 adds an error-analysis prompt, revises generation prompts, and discloses annotation labor, additional annotator qualifications, and submission-pool size. It omits v1's explicit temperature of 0.2, detailed provenance disclosure, and code-release commitment. It also announces a planned UniCode-Multi release; actual resource availability is not established.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around reasoning robustness, structural augmentation, and open-ended evaluation, adding discussions of works such as GSM-Plus, GSM-Symbolic, and WizardCoder. The biological-evolution motivation and its supporting references are removed. This changes the claimed relationship to prior research beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology narrative, results discussion, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Sections are reorganized, examples condensed, and the former Appendices A–H regrouped into experimental diagnostics and technical implementation appendices.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main text, replaces the introductory illustration with a multipanel overview, and adds variant-performance, error, case-study, and recursive-evaluation figures. The leaderboard gains a redesigned metric structure and cost column; new analysis tables appear, retained displays move, and the rating-interface illustration is split.

improvement.justification: V2 improves diagnostic usefulness through failure analyses and empirical checks of previously untested suite-composition and generator choices (Section 5; Appendices B.2–B.4). The net gain is limited by omitted temperature/provenance information, conflicting generator descriptions for the retained leaderboard, and stronger causal and contamination-related interpretations than the comparisons establish. The additional evidence helps, but does not fully resolve reproducibility and claim-support concerns.
